attachments.title: Source clinical note
attachments.text:
ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-07-15
Provider: Dr. Marcus Rodriguez, MD
Department: Hematology and Oncology
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Heavy and prolonged menstrual bleeding since menarche

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient presents to Hematology and Oncology for evaluation of heavy and prolonged menstrual bleeding, following her prior evaluation in January 2020 for frequent and prolonged nosebleeds. Since menarche at age 12, her periods have consistently lasted 8–10 days, and she reports soaking through pads every 1–2 hours on the heaviest days. She often passes large clots and occasionally feels lightheaded or fatigued during her cycles. She also experiences frequent spontaneous nosebleeds that can last up to 15 minutes and are difficult to control with pressure alone. Her mother notes that the patient bruises easily, often developing noticeable bruises on her arms and legs after minor bumps or pressure. The patient denies joint pain, swelling, or any history of deep muscle bleeding. Last year, she bled significantly following a routine dental cleaning and needed several hours of gauze packing to stop the bleeding.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Von Willebrand disease (diagnosed 2020-01-15)

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
She has not undergone any surgeries

MEDICATIONS:
She is not currently taking any medications or supplements.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
Her father had similar bleeding symptoms in adolescence, including frequent nosebleeds and prolonged bleeding after dental work, though he was never formally evaluated.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: 8th grade student.

VITAL SIGNS:
Vital signs are within normal limits.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, she appears well-developed and in no acute distress. She has scattered ecchymoses on her lower legs, but no petechiae, purpura, or joint abnormalities. There is no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly.

LABORATORY DATA:
A ristocetin cofactor assay is abnormal.

Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Behavioral changes, irritability, and loss of interest in activities

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 14-year-old female with Von Willebrand disease previously evaluated by Medical Genetics and Hematology/Oncology, who presents with behavioral changes. Over the past 3 months, she has become increasingly irritable, has frequent outbursts at home, and her grades have dropped significantly. She no longer enjoys playing soccer, which was previously her favorite activity. Her appetite has decreased, and she has trouble falling asleep.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:

FAMILY HISTORY:

Provider: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
Department: Medical Genetics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Frequent and prolonged nosebleeds over the past year

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The episodes typically occur spontaneously and last 10 to 20 minutes despite compression. The patient also reports heavy menstrual periods lasting over 7 days, often with large clots and occasional lightheadedness.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Her dentist previously noted prolonged bleeding after a cleaning.
The patient is otherwise healthy

PAST SURGICAL HISTORY:
She has no history of surgery,

MEDICATIONS:
She takes no medications.

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
Her father had similar nosebleeds in his youth and required cauterization. Her younger brother has no symptoms.

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: 8th grade student.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
There is no history of bruising, petechiae, or joint swelling.

VITAL SIGNS:
Vital signs are normal,

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
Exam reveals no abnormalities.

LABORATORY DATA:
Her complete blood count is within normal limits, and coagulation studies show a normal PT and aPTT.
